data.text: The Token Compute Principle Behind Chain-of-Thought

In autoregressive transformers, computation is strictly tied to token generation: each generated token represents one forward pass through all attention layers. If you ask a model a complex multi-step logical question and demand an immediate answer in a single token, the model has only one forward pass of compute to solve it. Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting prompts the model to generate intermediate reasoning steps ('thinking tokens') before producing the final conclusion, effectively expanding the computational capacity applied to the problem.

data.text: Working with Frontier Reasoning Models (o1 / o3-mini)

data.title: Reasoning Model Best Practices in .NET
data.text: When using models like OpenAI o1 or o3-mini: 1) Do NOT prompt 'think step by step'—these models already reason internally by default; doing so degrades performance. 2) System prompts are replaced with 'developer' messages. 3) You cannot set Temperature (it is fixed at 1.0). 4) Always allow generous max token limits because internal reasoning tokens consume the completion token budget.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Chain-of-Thought grants the model extra token passes to compute intermediate logic
Zero-shot CoT ('Think step by step') dramatically boosts multi-step reasoning accuracy
Self-Consistency samples multiple diverse reasoning paths and selects the statistical majority vote
Frontier reasoning models (o1 / o3-mini) generate internal reasoning tokens automatically
Account for internal reasoning tokens in latency budgets and cost monitoring dashboards
data.takeaway: Reasoning is token computation. Guiding models through structured step-by-step thinking or using native reasoning models unlocks reliable solutions to complex enterprise problems.
